01-golden-chain-story:
In 1263, Pope Urban IV asked Thomas Aquinas for a commentary on the Gospels. Instead of just writing his own thoughts, Thomas went verse by verse and gathered what more than 80 Church Fathers had said about each line.

They called it the Catena Aurea: the Golden Chain. Each saint a link, holding on to the one before, all the way back to the apostles.

We built Golden Chain so you can read the Bible the same way: tap any verse and see what Augustine, Chrysostom, Jerome and Aquinas said about it. Daily Mass readings, the whole Catechism in plain English, prayers and groups too.

Free. No ads. Made in South Africa. Link in bio.

Welcome, you're a link in the chain now.

03-ask-aquinas-anger:
Is it a sin to be angry? Aquinas answers in Summa Theologiae II-II, q.158, a.1.

Short version: anger is a passion, not a sin in itself. It goes wrong when it wants the wrong thing, or when it's out of proportion to what right reason calls for. Anger at injustice, kept in line by reason, can be good, and too little anger at evil is a fault too.

04-fathers-eucharist:
What did the first Christians believe about the Eucharist? Not "just a symbol".

St Ignatius of Antioch (c. AD 107), a disciple of the apostle John, called it "the flesh of our Saviour Jesus Christ" and "the medicine of immortality". St Justin Martyr (c. AD 155) wrote that Christians received it "not as common bread and common drink".

05-purgatory-explained:
November is the month of the Holy Souls. So: what is Purgatory, actually?

Not a second chance, and not a halfway house between heaven and hell. It's the final purification of those who die in God's friendship, so they're completely ready for heaven (CCC 1030).

The Church has always prayed for the dead (2 Maccabees 12:46). St Monica's last request to St Augustine was simply: "remember me at the altar of the Lord."

Pray for someone you've lost this week. Eternal rest grant unto them, O Lord. 🕯️

06-virtue-is-a-habit:
Aquinas called it virtue. Psychologists call it habit.

For Thomas, a virtue is a habitus: a stable disposition built by repeating good acts until doing good becomes easier and even joyful (ST I-II q.55). In 2010 a UCL study (Lally et al.) found new behaviours took 66 days on average to become automatic, anywhere from 18 to 254.

The difference: habits make you efficient. Virtue makes you free, with grace doing what willpower can't.

Pick one prayer. Same time every day. 66 days. Track it in Golden Chain → Prayers → My day.

How to pray when your mind won't shut up.

Around 1150 a Carthusian monk, Guigo II, described prayer as a ladder with four rungs: read, chew, talk, rest (lectio, meditatio, oratio, contemplatio).

Your mind will wander. Coming back is the prayer.

His classmates called Thomas Aquinas "the Dumb Ox." 🐂

He was big, quiet and never spoke up in class. Then his teacher, St Albert the Great, heard him argue a disputed question and said: "We call him the Dumb Ox, but one day his bellowing will be heard throughout the world."

Today (15 Nov) is the feast of St Albert: Dominican, bishop, scientist, and patron of scientists.

13-is-anxiety-a-sin:
"Is it a sin that I feel anxious?"

No. Aquinas calls fear and sadness passions: movements of the heart that happen to us. They aren't good or evil in themselves. What matters is what we do with them.

When Paul says "do not be anxious" (Phil 4:6), he isn't scolding a feeling. He's telling you where to bring it.

And if anxiety is taking over your sleep, eating or studies, please talk to a doctor, psychologist or your campus counselling centre. Getting help is not a lack of faith. Grace builds on nature.

Save this for a bad night. 🤍

15-why-confession:
"Why can't I just confess straight to God?"

You can, and you should. But Christ also gave his apostles a ministry that only works if they hear sins: "If you forgive the sins of any, they are forgiven" (John 20:23).

Confession gives you the words "I absolve you" out loud, breaks the secrecy where shame grows, and really forgives.

The seal is absolute. The priest has heard worse. The door is the same. So is the welcome.

The saint who made a joke while being executed. 🔥

He is now the patron saint of cooks and comedians. Tag the friend who burns the boerewors.

17-christ-the-king:
Why does the Church celebrate Christ the King?

Pope Pius XI created the feast in 1925 (Quas Primas), after a world war and with totalitarian movements on the rise. When societies push Christ out, they don't become neutral. Something else takes the throne.

His kingship is not of this world. His crown is thorns. His throne is a cross.

20-not-worthy:
Why do we say "under my roof" before Communion?

It's a quote, from a pagan Roman officer: "Lord, I am not worthy to have you come under my roof; but only say the word..." (Matthew 8:8). Jesus said he had never found such faith in Israel.

At every Mass you borrow a soldier's words: honest about your unworthiness, confident in His word. That is exactly what faith is.

25-dostoevsky-love-in-action:
"The more I love humanity in general, the less I love man in particular."

Dostoevsky put this confession in The Brothers Karamazov, and it might be the most relatable line in Russian literature. It's easy to love humanity. It's hard to love your roommate.

Father Zosima's answer: "Love in action is a harsh and dreadful thing compared with love in dreams." Aquinas would agree. Love is willing the good of a real person, not a feeling about everyone.

29-made-for-another-world:
Why does nothing quite satisfy?

C.S. Lewis: "If I find in myself a desire which no experience in this world can satisfy, the most probable explanation is that I was made for another world."

Aquinas got there 700 years earlier: he tests wealth, honour, fame, power and pleasure, and concludes only God can satisfy a desire for infinite good (ST I-II q.2 a.8).

The ache isn't a sign you're doing life wrong. It's a signpost. And Advent is the season of exactly this longing.

30-immaculate-conception:
Most Catholics get this one wrong: the Immaculate Conception is not about Jesus' conception. It's about Mary's.

From the first moment of her existence, Mary was preserved from original sin, by grace, because of the merits of Christ (Pius IX, 1854; CCC 491).

Twist for Thomists: Aquinas himself hesitated on this. Bl. John Duns Scotus answered his worry: Mary was saved too, by prevention rather than cure.

O Mary, conceived without sin, pray for us who have recourse to thee. 💙

32-stumbled-into-existence:
You think the perfect laws of reality just stumbled into existence?

One number: 1 in 10^(10^123). That is Nobel laureate Sir Roger Penrose's calculation of how precisely the universe's starting state had to be set (The Emperor's New Mind, 1989).

To be fair: Penrose is not a believer and doesn't claim this proves God. He proposes a cyclic universe; others propose a multiverse. But every serious answer agrees on one thing: this needs an explanation.

Aquinas' Fifth Way saw it 750 years ago: order points to mind (ST I, q.2, a.3).

Evidence, not a maths proof. Save this for the next time someone says "it just happened".

34-big-bang-priest:
The Big Bang theory was first proposed by a Catholic priest.

Fr Georges Lemaître showed in 1927 that Einstein's equations imply an expanding universe, and in 1931 proposed it began from a "primeval atom". Einstein's first reaction, as Lemaître recalled it: "Your calculations are correct, but your physics is abominable." He came round.

And the priest was the careful one: when Pius XII spoke in 1951 as if the theory confirmed Genesis, Lemaître urged caution. Creation means the universe depends on God at every moment, not only the first (Aquinas, ST I, q.46, a.2).

Faith and science were never enemies. Send this to someone who thinks they are.

36-universe-speaks-maths:
Why does the universe obey maths? Nobody ordered it to.

Equations on paper predicted Neptune, antimatter, gravitational waves and the Higgs boson before anyone saw them. Nobel physicist Eugene Wigner called this a "miracle" and "a wonderful gift which we neither understand nor deserve" (1960). Einstein: "The eternal mystery of the world is its comprehensibility" (1936).

Neither was arguing for Christianity. But Christians have an answer they don't: "In the beginning was the Logos" (John 1:1). Word, and reason. A universe that comes from Mind is readable by minds.

This doesn't prove the faith. It shows which worldview isn't surprised.

38-something-rather-than-nothing:
Why is there something rather than nothing?

Everything you have ever met could have not existed. It borrows its existence from something else. A chain of borrowers, however long, still needs a lender. That is Aquinas' Third Way (ST I, q.2, a.3).

"But who made God?" The argument never said everything has a cause; it says everything that doesn't have to exist has one. God is not one more link in the chain. "I AM WHO AM" (Exodus 3:14).

"Physics says a universe can come from nothing"? A quantum vacuum with laws is not nothing.

You didn't have to exist. You do. Read the Five Ways in Golden Chain → Theology.

42-john-of-the-cross:
He wrote one of the greatest poems in Spanish in a prison cell.

In December 1577, friars who opposed the Carmelite reform locked St John of the Cross in a tiny cell in Toledo. In the dark he composed the first stanzas of the Spiritual Canticle. After about nine months he escaped down the wall on a rope of knotted blankets.

His "dark night" is not simply sadness: it is God teaching the soul to love him and not only his gifts. (It is not a name for depression, which deserves real care and real help.)

"In the evening of life, we will be judged on love alone."

Feast: 14 December.

49-st-martin-cloak:
He cut it in half.

Amiens, winter, around AD 335. Martin is a young Roman cavalry officer, not yet baptised. At the city gate a freezing man is begging and everyone walks past. Martin has nothing left to give but his cloak, so he draws his sword, cuts it in two and gives away half.

That night he dreams of Christ wearing the half-cloak and saying to the angels: "Martin, still only a catechumen, has clothed me with this robe" (Sulpicius Severus, Life of St Martin, 3).

And the cloak outlived him. The Frankish kings kept it as a relic; the shrine that held it was the capella. Every chapel and every chaplain is named after half a coat.

Feast: 11 November. You don't need much to give. Half will do.

Art: El Greco, Saint Martin and the Beggar, 1597/99. National Gallery of Art, Washington (Open Access).

50-aura-check:
Aura check: saints edition.

Daniel got thrown to the lions and it was the king who couldn't sleep. Joan of Arc, nineteen and without a lawyer, answered a trick question so well her judges were stunned. Paul survived floggings, a stoning and three shipwrecks, then wrote "Rejoice" from prison. Polycarp, aged 86, was offered his life to curse Christ and declined.

Painters drew it as a ring of gold. Aquinas calls it fortitude: a firm mind when doing good gets costly.
